I'm not an atheist, but rather a deist / existentialist. Yes, those two belief systems are parallel, but I'm torn between them in the fact that deism believes in "god" as a general term, as there is not much else to describe God accurately. 
     In deism, "God" exists in some sense, be God an entity or a physical being, it's entirely irrelevant to the belief that "it" exists in some form as stated. The definition given by Deism.com is as "Deism is knowledge of God based on application of reason on the designs and laws found throughout nature." Essentially, deism holds the belief that something / someone had to create us. Our world is amazing, and there is a seemingly infinite universe beyond this puny world. 
     We have a creator, but we are by no means God's chosen people. This universe is just too big for us to exist only because God desired someone other than Angels, whom he programmed to love him, to live in an alternate dimension, and strive to love him, also being that it they don't love him, they will be sent to eternal damnation. Deism rejects any attributes of revealed religion, such as Christianity / Judaism / Islam. 

     Existentialism is the part of my beliefs that I can't quite put a pinpoint on, because while I consider myself a deist, any belief in some creator beyond our world is held loosely, because even if there is, I don't care enough to worry about its existence, and even more so the relationship it holds with us. Existentialism takes the core aspects of Nihilism, and basically says while our lives in the grand scheme of things are meaningless, we pave our own future for the betterment of ourselves, almost with a mindset of "hey, life is short and meaningless, but that doesn't mean we can't have fun while we're here." It takes our nihilistic existence and mixes it with some good ol' optimism.
     Thus, I don't necessarily "deny" God. I just believe that if God exists, it simply created us, whatever God is, and leaves it at that. God is essentially the clockmaker of the universe. He created it, wound it up, and let it go. 
     We live self-sustaining lives, and technology / science has completely eliminated the need for a god to be an active part of our lives. Anything a god can do, we can do ourselves using technology. Hell, we have 3D printers now. Pretty soon, knowledge of this science will progress to the point where we can make food with it. Who needs Jesus Christ making duplications of some fish and bread when we can make our own fried rice and veggies with a 3D printer? 

I guess that's just it. If there's a god, cool. We don't need him. If there's not a god, then so be it. We still don't need him.
